title: Camp 2 close: one light, ten lamps
hook: Sikhs speak of one light passing through all ten Gurus, and now resting in the Granth and the Khalsa

segments.voice: Yesterday, the needle for the next world, and Duni Chand's flags. Your line was what goes with you. Did the needle's question stop you once? Day ninety-six.

At a candlelight vigil, one person lights a candle, then tips it toward the next person's wick. That one lights the next, and the next, down the whole line, until the dark street is full of small flames. Watch closely and there's something strange. The first flame never gets smaller. Nothing is taken from it. The light just keeps going. For seventy-five days you've walked through the Sikh story, from a boy born at Talwandi to a Guru bowing before a book at Nanded. Ten Gurus. Sikhs have one word for what connects them all, and it's the word for that flame.
screen: `ONE CANDLE LIGHTS THE NEXT.` → `THE FIRST FLAME NEVER SHRINKS.` → `TEN GURUS, ONE WORD.`

segments.voice: Jot. Light, flame, the light of the divine. Sikhs say there were ten Gurus in body, but one light. It's in the Guru Granth Sahib itself. Two musicians at Guru Arjan's court, Satta and Balwand, sang that the light was the same and the way was the same; only the body changed. Nanak's light in Angad, then in Amar Das, then Ram Das, all the way to Gobind Singh. When a Guru died, Sikhs didn't say he was gone. They said his light merged back into the light. And at Nanded the light didn't go out. It came to rest in two places: the Guru Granth Sahib, and the Khalsa, the community gathered. Look back at what that light did in this camp. Sacha sauda, the true bargain of feeding the hungry. Mardana's rebab, the travels, Kartarpur. Angad's ang, the wrestling ground, the baoli at Goindwal. The Anand, Amritsar, the four rounds of the lavan. Harmandir Sahib, the Adi Granth, Guru Arjan's martyrdom. Miri piri and the Akal Takht. A child Guru, a Guru who gave his head in Chandni Chowk. Vaisakhi, the Panj Pyare, amrit, the Khalsa. The Sahibzade, the Chali Mukte, the Zafarnama. Ten lamps, and the same flame in every one. And the Gurus say that flame isn't only in them. In the evening prayer, Kirtan Sohila, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase, that in everyone there is a light, and that light is the One. The stories are told. Now the next camp turns to what the light asks you to do with your hands.
screen: `JOT — LIGHT, FLAME.` · `ONLY THE BODY CHANGED.` · `RESTING IN THE GRANTH AND THE KHALSA.` · `A LIGHT IN EVERYONE.` · then, large: `ONE LIGHT, TEN LAMPS.`

segments.voice: If you can, light a lamp or a candle, somewhere safe. If you can't, look at any small light near you, or picture one. Watch the flame. It's never still, and never quite the same shape twice, and yet it's the same flame. Breathe slowly and let your eyes rest there. Think of one person whose light reached you: a parent, a teacher, a friend. Their flame lit yours, and it didn't get smaller. The bell holds the time.
Jot. The divine light, one flame through all ten Gurus, now resting in the Granth and the Khalsa. Camp two is complete.
Your line: one light, ten lamps. Today, notice one light in someone else, and tell them. Tomorrow, camp three: the practices, starting with seva. Day ninety-six.

howItsDone: Sikhs honor the ten Gurus as one light in ten forms, and mark each Guru's birth and passing with gurpurabs; when speaking of a Guru's death they often say he merged into the divine light.

fork.setup: you're lighting candles at a vigil, one flame to the next. after you light ten others, what's happened to your own flame?
options: it has grown weaker with each one.
fork.reveal: a flame loses nothing by lighting another. Sikhs use the picture of one light passing through ten Gurus.

original.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: the light, as the Guru Granth Sahib spells it; everyday Punjabi writes it ਜੋਤ.

trapdoor: what you thought: a word for a flame.
what it means: the one divine light Sikhs say passed through all ten Gurus and lives in everyone.
what a scholar hears: Satta and Balwand's Var (Ang 966) sings the same light in each Guru, only the body changing; Kirtan Sohila (Ang 13) puts that light in all.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 966 (Var of Satta and Balwand, Raag Ramkali: the same light, the same way, only the body changed)
Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 13 (Kirtan Sohila, Guru Nanak: in all is the light, and that light is the One)

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer opens 'Picture' and no longer tells the listener what they notice; cut the rounded 'two hundred and forty years', the baoli's 'eighty-four steps' and 'the first shaheed' (count and superlative not in today's cited text); 'a Guru at five' now 'a child Guru'. The earlier note on the 239-year rounding is now moot.
Camp 2 summary lists the camp's words and stories from the index (days 22-95); confirm selection.
Ang 966 (joti oha jugati sai sahi kaia pher paltiai) paraphrased; confirm Ang and attribution to Satta and Balwand.
Ang 13 (sabh mahi joti joti hai soi) paraphrased; confirm.
'Merged back into the light' reflects the idiom joti jot samaana; confirm.
'Two hundred and forty years' spans 1469 to 1708 (239 years); confirm the rounding.
Original: ਜੋਤਿ as spelled in scripture vs ਜੋਤ in modern Punjabi; confirm the note and pronunciation hint.
